questions.text: Trench warfare on the Western Front defined which conflict?
questions.explanation: Millions of soldiers lived and fought in trench lines across France and Belgium from 1914 to 1918.

questions.text: Which wall, built in 1961, divided East and West Berlin until it was opened in 1989?
questions.explanation: The Berlin Wall split East and West Berlin until it was opened in November 1989.

questions.text: Who led Britain as Prime Minister for most of World War II?
questions.explanation: Churchill became Prime Minister in May 1940 and led the wartime coalition until 1945.

questions.text: In which year did Germany surrender, ending World War II in Europe?
questions.explanation: Germany surrendered in May 1945, celebrated as VE Day.

questions.text: Which country did Germany invade in September 1939, leading Britain and France to declare war?
questions.explanation: The invasion of Poland on 1 September 1939 triggered the declarations of war.

questions.text: Operation Overlord was the Allied invasion of which French region in 1944?
questions.explanation: Overlord launched on D-Day, 6 June 1944, with landings on the Normandy beaches.

questions.text: Which 1919 treaty imposed reparations on Germany after World War I?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in June 1919 and included the war guilt and reparations clauses.

questions.text: Whose assassination in Sarajevo in 1914 set off the chain of events leading to World War I?
questions.explanation: Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne, was shot on 28 June 1914.

questions.text: Which battle of 1942-43 ended with the surrender of Germany's Sixth Army?
questions.explanation: The German Sixth Army surrendered at Stalingrad in early 1943, a major turning point on the Eastern Front.

questions.text: Which US president authorised the atomic bombs dropped on Japan in 1945?
questions.explanation: Truman had become president after Roosevelt's death in April 1945.

questions.text: Which Soviet leader introduced the policies of glasnost and perestroika?
questions.explanation: Gorbachev led the USSR from 1985 and launched these openness and restructuring reforms.

questions.text: The February 1945 Yalta Conference brought together Churchill, Stalin and which other leader?
questions.explanation: Roosevelt attended Yalta shortly before his death in April 1945.

questions.text: Which June 1942 naval battle saw US carrier aircraft sink four Japanese aircraft carriers?
questions.explanation: At Midway the US sank Akagi, Kaga, Soryu and Hiryu, shifting the Pacific balance.

questions.text: Which battle began on 1 July 1916 with the British Army's heaviest single-day casualties?
questions.explanation: The first day of the Somme cost the British Army roughly 57,000 casualties.

questions.text: Which 1939 agreement between Germany and the USSR contained a secret protocol dividing Eastern Europe?
questions.explanation: The non-aggression pact of August 1939 secretly carved up Poland and the Baltic region.

spares.text: Alongside Britain and the United States, which communist state was a major Allied power in World War II?
spares.explanation: The USSR joined the Allies after being invaded by Germany in June 1941.

spares.text: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
spares.explanation: The border was opened on 9 November 1989.

spares.text: The Armistice ending WWI fighting was signed in a railway carriage in a forest near which French town?
spares.explanation: The armistice took effect at 11 a.m. on 11 November 1918.

spares.text: Which 1941 charter, agreed by Roosevelt and Churchill off Newfoundland, set out shared post-war aims?
spares.explanation: The Atlantic Charter was announced in August 1941 and later influenced the United Nations.
